segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And they captured Joscelin,
and brought him to Nur al-Din, the lord of Aleppo.
And he bought him from them for a thousand dinars,
and cast him into chains and imprisoned him.
And he remained in prison for nine years,
while they continually enticed him to apostatize by promises and threats,
but he did not yield,
but persevered while confessing
that on account of his sins—
because he had plundered the monastery of Mar Bar Sawma,
as we show, by God's help, in the Ecclesiastical [History]—
the Lord had chastised him.
And when his death drew near,
he made a request, and they brought the bishop of the city to him;
and he made confession,
and he administered the Holy Mysteries to him.
And there, in the pit, he ended his life.
And when Joscelin was imprisoned,
the Turks took greater courage,
and captured many places from the Franks:
Gargar and Kakhti (or Gakhti? And also Hisn Mansur and Teginkar and Tegnakar) which are beside the monastery.
As for the Franks who were in Tell Bashir,
when Joscelin fell,
they set up {OCR?} in his place his young son,
who was also called Joscelin.
And in the year 1461
—1461 of the Greeks—
when the people of Kaysum saw the might of the Turks,
they sent the bishop, Mar Iwannis, to Mas'ud, the Sultan of Iconium,
and took a pledge for the Franks who were with them,
that they might depart in peace to Ayntab.
And this did take place.
And that Sultan of Iconium took possession of Kaysum, and the fortress area, and Ra'ban, and Farzaman, and Mar'ash.
And when he encamped against Tell Bashir,
Nur al-Din, son of Zengi, came to him,
and the Sultan gave his daughter to Nur al-Din as a wife.
And he left Tell Bashir and departed,
because he was not able to capture it.
Then the King of Jerusalem came {OCR?},
and brought out the wife of Joscelin, and his sons, and all the Franks,
and took them to Jerusalem;
and he placed in Tell Bashir men belonging to the King of the Greeks.
And these Greeks also took control of Ayntab and 'Azaz.
And afterwards,
when Nur al-Din pressed hard against them both with battles and with famine,
they surrendered these places to him peacefully.
And Timurtash, the lord of Mardin, gained control over Bireh, Samosata, Kouris, and Kfarsut.
And in Qal'ah Rumayta
there was an Armenian man whose name was Michael.
